criteria.text: Hyperphagia in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome (FDA indication).
Patient is at least 4 years old (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an endocrinologist or geneticist (approval criterion 2).
Prader-Willi syndrome diagnosis confirmed by genetic testing indicating chromosome 15 mutation (approval criterion 3).
History of hypersensitivity to diazoxide or thiazides (denial criterion 2).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid VykatTM XR (brand Vykat XR; diazoxide choline), an ATP-sensitive potassium channel activator / hyperphagia agent. Version 1; Original 10/13/2025; Accepted 11/21/2025; Effective 01/01/2026.
Encoded: closed FDA indication, approval criteria 1-4 and hypersensitivity denial criterion 2. Denial criterion 1 (failure to meet approval criteria) is represented by the approval predicates.

Cautions (notes only): monitor hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and fasting glucose prior to and throughout treatment; dose adjustment may be necessary with strong CYP1A2 inhibitors; edema, including severe reactions associated with fluid overload, has been reported.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization approval up to one year.

Quantity (notes only): 25 mg tablets: 120 tablets/30 days; 75 mg tablets: 210 tablets/30 days; 150 mg tablets: 90 tablets/30 days. Total cumulative dose must not exceed FDA label recommended weight-based target dose. max_units is null.

Genetic confirmation and hyperphagia are attestations. Documentation verification, monitoring, dose adjustment, duration and quantity enforcement require manual review; this pack remains partial. PDL status unknown; no linked alternatives.
